items.stem: The principle of indemnity means insurance aims to:

options.text: Restore the insured to their position before the loss, not better
options.rationale: Correct: indemnity restores, it does not enrich.

options.text: Pay the insured more than the loss as a reward
options.rationale: Profiting from a loss breaches indemnity.

options.text: Pay a fixed amount regardless of the loss
options.rationale: That describes certain benefit policies, not the indemnity principle.

options.text: Refund all premiums if no claim is made
options.rationale: Premiums are the cost of cover, not refundable by default.

items.explanation: Correct: indemnity restores, it does not enrich.
items.provenance: original Mastemy item drafted by an AI agent; no external question source

items.stem: Which two must generally be true for a valid insurance contract? (Select TWO)

options.text: The insured has an insurable interest in the subject
Material facts are disclosed in good faith
options.rationale: Correct: utmost good faith / disclosure is required.

options.text: The insured is guaranteed to make a claim
options.rationale: No claim is guaranteed or required.

options.text: The policy pays out even for deliberately caused losses
options.rationale: Deliberate self-inflicted loss is typically excluded.

items.stem: A policy has a sum insured of 10,000 and an excess of 500. A covered loss of 3,000 would pay:

options.rationale: Correct: the insurer pays the loss less the 500 excess.
500 is the excess retained by the insured, not the payout.
The sum insured is a ceiling, not the payout for a 3,000 loss.

items.explanation: Correct: the insurer pays the loss less the 500 excess.
